title: UI Conductor weekly capture: rollout telemetry, spike, and quick mitigations
content:
Date: 2026-08-03
Owners: Priya, Ethan, Samira, Jonas, Maya
Channel: #console-rollouts (Slack)
Meeting length: 25m (quick capture format)

Purpose: fast weekly capture focused on the ongoing "UI Conductor" partial rollout (canary -> 20% -> 100%), recent telemetry spike, and small mitigations we can ship quickly to reduce surface area. This doc is a working log; actionable items at the bottom.

Attendees and quick mood check:
- Priya N: focused on telemetry, investigating KV cache hits
- Ethan M: UI perf and CDN routing changes
- Samira V: rollout strategy and flags coordination with infra
- Jonas B: analytics queries and evaluation of sample bias
- Maya C: QA and regression verification (manual checks)

What shipped / recent changes (last 7 days):
- Flipped canary for UI Conductor to 8% traffic yesterday (RINF-3097).
- CDN edge routing change rolled for canary only (PR #1486). Observed small reduce in TTFB for some regions.
- Added lightweight telemetry tags to identify path permutations that exercise new rollout code paths.

Current signals and concerns:
- Telemetry spike: between 10:40–11:10 PDT yesterday we saw a p95 page-load increase from ~210ms -> ~480ms for canary cohort. Not seen in stable. (Samira traced to two buckets: cache miss storm for KV prefix X, and a small increase in upstream inference tail latency from dedicated-backend pool.)
- Error surface: client JS error rate up 0.03% (from 0.01%) within canary sessions. Stack indicates failure to parse new feature flag metadata when network request returned 500.
- Analytics sampling: current dashboards undercount canary because some telemetry events were filtered by an older pipeline rule. Jonas is retrofitting a one-off query to rehydrate the last 24h events for accurate assessment.

Root-cause hypotheses in-flight:
1) Cache warmup + simultaneous TTL expirations (KV prefix X) caused N extra backend calls during a tight window, cascading into higher tail latency.
2) A small race in feature flag fetch code path fails gracefully in stable but surfaces in canary due to different response shape from the new rollout service.
3) Edge routing for new CDN variant exposes a region with slightly worse peering — exacerbating p95 for some users.

Immediate mitigations discussed (short, low-risk ops):
- Roll back CDN variant for the canary cohort only (Ethan) — if p95 improves by >30% within 30m hold, proceed to re-evaluate. (Action: Ethan, ETA 1h)
- Deploy a fix to defensive feature-flag parsing to avoid throwing on unexpected server shapes (Priya to ship hotfix behind flag). (Action: Priya, ETA 4h)
- Temporary increase canary sampling to 4% while we gather more telemetry (Samira to coordinate), but only after rollback if CDN is culprit. This helps accelerate data collection for the parsing fix test matrix. (Action: Samira, ETA 6h)
- Short-term: add low-cardinality tag to telemetry to group by CDN variant + region so analytics can slice quickly. (Action: Jonas, ETA 2h)

Longer-term follow-ups (backlog / non-blocking):
- Rewrite KV prefix eviction to add jitter and improve cache warming strategy; partner with infra. (Ticket: RINF-3120)
- Add end-to-end synthetic checks scoped to canary paths to detect cache storms and upstream latency before user-facing impact.
- Improve feature flag schema validation on client + server to avoid schema drift issues.

Observations from QA (Maya):
- Manual walk-throughs: two paths where client throws a console error when flag metadata missing — cosmetic but loud on Sentry. Repro steps attached in ticket.
- Regression checklist: smoke tests passed on stable build; failures only reproduce consistently when using the canary CDN variant and enabling the new rollout flag.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- If rollback reduces p95 but parsing fix also appears to help, do we reintroduce CDN variant behind a stricter circuit breaker? (Samira to propose threshold rules.)
- Should canary cohort be split by region to isolate peering issues? (Pros: easier signal; Cons: slower coverage.)

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Ethan: rollback CDN variant for canary, monitor p95 & errors — 2026-08-03 11:45 PDT
- Priya: prepare and canary-deploy defensive parsing patch behind feature flag — 2026-08-03 15:00 PDT
- Jonas: run backfill query to rehydrate filtered events and add CDN+region slice to dashboards — 2026-08-03 13:00 PDT
- Samira: coordinate canary traffic adjustments and update rollout playbook with new circuit-breaker thresholds — 2026-08-03 EOD
- Maya: run focused QA matrix on canary after each change; capture repro clips for SRE and frontend — ongoing today

Notes to self / rough brainstorm (informal):
- We should add a small backoff jitter in client flag fetch (quick win).
- Consider a lightweight lease for KV prefix writes during high churn events to avoid stampedes.
- Would be nice to have a preflight simulation that replays 1h of user sessions against new code paths to catch cache storms — long-term project.

Meeting wrap / next check-in:
- This doc is the single source for today's quick decisions. If rollback happens, update the Slack thread and add a short blameless postmortem note to Confluence.
- Next synchronous: 2026-08-04 09:30 PDT (short follow-up) or earlier if hotfix deployed.

Links / references: RINF-3097 (current rollout), RINF-3120 (cache strategy), PR #1486 (CDN routing), Confluence: Console-Rollout-Playbook.

Status: working notes; will convert to postmortem draft if incident persists.
